chalisa.do1: A sweet flute graces his hand, and his body is dark like a blue rain-cloud. His red lips are like the bimba fruit, and his lotus eyes are delightful.
chalisa.do2: His face is like the full moon and the lotus, and the yellow garment is his fine attire. Victory to Kṛṣṇacandra Mahārāja, enchanter of hearts, with the beauty of Madana, the god of love.
chalisa.cau1: Victory to the joy of the Yadus, victory to the one the world worships; victory to the son of Vasudeva and Devakī. ॥1॥
chalisa.cau2: Victory to Yaśodā's son, Nanda's darling; victory to the Lord, the apple of the devotees' eyes. ॥2॥
chalisa.cau3: Victory to the master dancer, who reined in the serpent, Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā, who grazes the cows. ॥3॥
chalisa.cau4: Lord, once more hold up the great mountain on your fingernail; come and take away the hardships of the humble. ॥4॥
chalisa.cau5: Setting the flute to your lips, you sounded its sweet call; may this prayer of mine be fulfilled. ॥5॥
chalisa.cau6: Come, Hari, taste butter once again; today protect the honour of Bhārata. ॥6॥
chalisa.cau7: Your cheeks are round and your chin is rosy; your gentle smile casts a spell. ॥7॥
chalisa.cau8: Your large eyes are like tinted lotuses; you wear a crown of peacock feathers and the vaijayantī garland. ॥8॥
chalisa.cau9: Earrings are in your ears, and you wear a fine yellow garment; a belt of little bells is at your waist, and your dhoti is tucked up as a kāchnī. ॥9॥
chalisa.cau10: Your handsome body shines like a blue lotus; seeing its beauty, gods, men and sages are enchanted at heart. ॥10॥
chalisa.cau11: A tilaka is on your forehead, and your locks are curly. Come, Kṛṣṇa, player of the flute. ॥11॥
chalisa.cau12: Drinking her milk, you gave Pūtanā liberation, and you slew Agha, Baka and Kāgāsura. ॥12॥
chalisa.cau13: When Madhuvana was burning in the flames of a fire, the flames grew cool as soon as Nanda's darling looked at them. ॥13॥
chalisa.cau14: When Indra, lord of the gods, came against Braj in anger and rained down water in torrents thick as pestles, ॥14॥
chalisa.cau15: and, keeping it up, sought to sweep Braj away, you held up Govardhana on your fingernail and saved it. ॥15॥
chalisa.cau16: Seeing it, Yaśodā was greatly bewildered in mind, when you showed the fourteen worlds in your mouth. ॥16॥
chalisa.cau17: Wicked Kaṃsa raised great havoc when he demanded ten million lotus flowers. ॥17॥
chalisa.cau18: Then you reined in Kāliya and, giving him the marks of your feet, made him fearless. ॥18॥
chalisa.cau19: You delighted in the rāsa dance with the gopīs and fulfilled the longing of them all. ॥19॥
chalisa.cau20: You destroyed many a great demon, and you seized Kaṃsa by the hair, dashed him down and killed him. ॥20॥
chalisa.cau21: You freed your mother and father from captivity and had the kingdom given to Ugrasena. ॥21॥
chalisa.cau22: You brought back all six dead sons from the earth and wiped away the sorrow of mother Devakī. ॥22॥
chalisa.cau23: You destroyed the demons Bhaumāsura and Mura and brought back sixteen thousand maidens. ॥23॥
chalisa.cau24: You gave Bhīma the sign for the slaying with a straw split in two, and Jarāsandha the demon was killed. ॥24॥
chalisa.cau25: You slew Bakāsura and other demons, and then took away the hardships of your devotees. ॥25॥
chalisa.cau26: You took away the sorrow of poor Sudāmā and put three handfuls of rice into your mouth. ॥26॥
chalisa.cau27: At Vidura's house you asked for greens offered in love, and you gave up Duryodhana's dried fruits. ॥27॥
chalisa.cau28: You saw the great glory of love; such is Śyāma, the friend of the humble. ॥28॥
chalisa.cau29: In the Bhārata war you drove Pārtha's chariot; you took up the discus in your hand, and your strength never tired. ॥29॥
chalisa.cau30: You imparted the knowledge of your Gītā and showered nectar into the hearts of devotees. ॥30॥
chalisa.cau31: Mīrā was so intoxicated with love that she drank the poison clapping her hands. ॥31॥
chalisa.cau32: The Rāṇā sent a snake in a basket, and Banavārī became a śālagrāma. ॥32॥
chalisa.cau33: You showed your māyā to Brahmā and wiped every doubt from his heart. ॥33॥
chalisa.cau34: Having reviled you a hundred times, Śiśupāla was at once set free from life. ॥34॥
chalisa.cau35: When Draupadī cried out: Lord of the lowly, my honour is going now, ॥35॥
chalisa.cau36: at once Nanda's darling became the garment; the cloth kept growing, and the enemies' faces were blackened with shame. ॥36॥
chalisa.cau37: Such is Kanhaiyā, lord of the helpless, who saves the boat sinking in the whirlpool. ॥37॥
chalisa.cau38: Sundardās holds hope in his heart; Banavārī, cast your merciful glance. ॥38॥
chalisa.cau39: Lord, take away all my evil thinking, and quickly forgive my offences. ॥39॥
chalisa.cau40: Open the curtain now and grant your darśana. Say: Victory to Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā! ॥40॥
chalisa.do3: Whoever recites this Chālīsā of Kṛṣṇa, holding it in the heart, gains as its fruit the eight siddhis, the nine treasures and the four goals of life.
